title: Welcome rituals and technical setup - 14day playbook
summary: A compact 14-day playbook focused on human rituals + technical setup to accelerate new hires from day 0 to productive contributor, with checklists for preboard, day0/1, week1, and week2 plus light buddy rubric and escalation pointers.
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a tactical companion for People Ops and hiring managers to ensure new joiners at Redwood Inference land culturally and technically during the first 14 days. Emphasis is on: predictable device & account readiness, small human rituals that build belonging, and a low-friction buddy program that surfaces blockers early.

How to use:
- People Ops owns preboarding items and vendor/device steps.
- Hiring manager + assigned buddy own cultural rituals and week-by-week goals.
- SRE/IT owns imaging, VPN, and KMS access.

Preboarding (ideally completed 3–5 business days before start)
- Confirm device order and imaging with IT; include hardware serial + expected ship date.
- Create directory in Drive for new hire: /shared_drives/company/misc/onboard-<name>-wk0 (People Ops).
- Provision Okta user, Slack account, Google Drive folder, and GCP/AWS test project access.
- Send welcome packet: org chart, first-week schedule, Slack channel invite, short culture notes (30–45 mins read).
- Assign buddy and schedule day0 30-min welcome call.
- Share minimal repo access (read) and a tiny first-week task with clear success criteria (e.g., run the local dev container and post a screenshot).

Day 0 / Day 1 checklist
- 48-hour device health check: IT confirms boot + MDM policy applied.
- Day0 30-min welcome with hiring manager: team overview, expectations, first-week goals.
- Buddy 30-min intro: coffee chat, Slack etiquette, where to ask quick questions.
- Access verification: Slack, Google Drive, Confluence, Jira/Linear, GitHub (read). If any backend tokens missing, escalate to IT with ticket template.
- One-liner task: run the dev container and open the ‘hello-inference’ example (aim for >1 success to build confidence).

Week 1: rituals + practicals (days 2–7)
- Ritual: Team standup cadence explained and observed; buddy ensures new hire gives their first update by Day 3.
- 1:1 cadence: schedule weekly 1:1 with manager; first 1:1 focused on psychological safety + role clarity.
- Team lunch/intro: asynchronous or in-person depending on location (People Ops organizes a virtual lunch room if remote).
- Security & compliance 20-min sync: KMS overview, data handling rules, and research exceptions.
- Micro-goal: complete two onboarding tickets: (a) run inference demo end-to-end, (b) submit a simple docs change to README.
- Weekly check: buddy completes the buddy rubric (see below) and shares with manager.

Week 2: acceleration (days 8–14)
- Ritual: Owner rotation — new hire leads a 10-min demo of what they learned to team.
- Remove soft blockers: confirm full access to any SaaS used by team (monitoring, buildkite, model catalog).
- Introduce rollout/ops runbook: short walkthrough of what to do when an endpoint misbehaves.
- Performance goal: contribute a small non-prod PR or run an inference performance micro-benchmark and record results.
- 14-day 1:1: manager and new hire review goals and set 30/60/90 plan. People Ops collects pulse feedback.

Buddy program quick rubric (one-page, lightweight — buddy fills at Day 7)
- Availability: Did buddy meet with hire at least 3x in week 1? (Yes/No)
- Practical help: Did buddy help resolve at least one blocker (access, local run, doc)? (Yes/No)
- Cultural orientation: Did buddy introduce hire to 2+ team rituals or informal channels? (Yes/No)
- Confidence signal: On a 1–5 scale, how confident does the buddy think the hire is in basic dev workflow? (1–5)
- Notes: free-form quick items (issues to escalate, wins).

Escalation & tickets
- Use JIRA-ONB for missing device imaging and IT escalations.
- Use SRE runbook channel (#sre-oncall) for infra-level network/VPN issues; copy People Ops for visibility.
- For security gating (KMS/HSM) open a compliance ticket and tag security@redwood.com.

Mini interview rubric for internal hiring decisions during probation (lightweight, used by manager + people ops)
- Role fit (technical): Evidence that the hire can complete core onboarding tasks (read repo, run examples). Options: Meets / Developing / Needs support.
- Collaboration: Attends rituals, asks clarifying questions, engages in reviews. Options: Meets / Developing / Needs support.
- Initiative: Takes on microtasks and seeks feedback. Options: Meets / Developing / Needs support.
- Safety net: If any category is ‘Needs support’ at 14 days, create a 30-day remediation plan with clear measurable checkpoints.

People Ops templates (copy/paste)
- Day0 email subject: "Welcome to Redwood — Day 0 logistics for <Name>"
- IT ticket template: "New hire imaging + access — Name, Role, Manager, Start Date, Shipping Address, Required SaaS"
- Buddy intro template (Slack): short script to DM a new hire and propose 3 quick sync times.

Open questions we iterate on:
- Should every new hire get a short production-read PR within 14 days? pros/cons.
- Ways to standardize the cultural rituals across remote-first pods without being prescriptive.

Appendix: quick checklist for managers (one screen)
- Confirm preboarding checklist completed (device, Okta, Slack, Drive).
- Schedule Day0 manager intro + Day0 buddy intro.
- Share first-week task and success criteria.
- Book 30-minute team demo in Week 2 for the hire.
- Fill buddy rubric Day 7 and review Day 14.

Notes and provenance:
- Drafted by Riley Chen (People Ops) with input from Eng managers Aisha K. and Jonah P.
- Built from prior onboarding notes and pilot run Q4 2024; we observed faster time-to-first-PR when dev container + one clear microtask shipped before day 3.

Contact: Riley Chen (people-ops) — riley.chen@redwood.com
footnotes: This is a living playbook — update after each hire cycle. Keep artifacts in the per-hire Drive folder and link to the new-hire pulse survey results.
